F129.title: Correspondence-messages path bypasses /media/presign entirely
F129.whatWasWrong: src/messages/messages.service.ts created Media at status=READY from a client-supplied storageKey with no ownership proof, no existence check, no MIME check and no size check.
F129.change: Added MediaService.verifyClientSuppliedObject — the governed door for callers who already hold a key. It answers the same three questions in the same vocabulary: WHO OWNS IT (keys are namespaced users/{userId}/ by makeObjectKey, so a key outside the caller's prefix is refused before storage is touched), DOES IT EXIST (headObject, so a row can never reach READY for bytes never uploaded), WHAT IS IT (size and content type taken from STORAGE, not the client's claim, checked against the same canonical MIME policy and size buckets presign uses).
F129.wiring: MessagesService now verifies every attachment BEFORE opening the database transaction — network I/O must not be held inside a transaction, and a refused attachment refuses the send rather than half-writing a message or silently dropping a file.
F129.deliberatelyNotDone: The full six-layer Content Truth resolution (magic bytes, container inspection) is NOT run here. That is confirmUpload's job and needs byte-range reads. Running it here would change what the product ACCEPTS on a currently-working path, which CH-11's destructive boundary and the RC-C5 preserve obligations forbid doing incidentally.
F129.preserveConstraintVerified: Every server-side key generator in the repository uses makeObjectKey(userId, ...) — presign (media.service.ts:388) and the multipart uploads controller (uploads.controller.ts:93,148). The ownership prefix check therefore narrows NO legitimate path. Verified by enumeration, not assumed.
F129.existingDataUntouched: The check applies at send time for new messages only. No existing Media or MessageAttachment row is read, rewritten or re-validated. No migration, no production-data mutation.
F129.newState: IMPLEMENTED_NOT_LIVE_CERTIFIED (not recorded into Stage-0 evidence — see stateHandling below)

F133.title: Duration unit mismatch — Media.duration is ms, MessageAttachment.durationSec is seconds
F133.whatWasWrong: messages.service.ts:238 wrote SECONDS into Media.duration (a millisecond column) and :752 read MILLISECONDS back out as durationSec (a seconds field). A 30-second voice note persisted as 30 ms and projected as 30000 seconds. Nothing crashed, which is why it survived.
F133.change: New src/media/duration-units.ts with durationSecondsToMillis / durationMillisToSeconds, so the conversion is NAMED at every call site and a bare assignment between the two fields looks wrong on sight. Both call sites converted.
F133.honestLimit: Rounding is to whole units because both columns are integers. Sub-second precision is not representable in durationSec and is not invented; the loss is recorded as a test rather than left as a surprise.

existingDataNotCorrected.statement: Rows already written with the wrong unit are NOT corrected. Fixing them is a production-data mutation and is not authorized.
existingDataNotCorrected.exposure: Historical correspondence attachments carry a Media.duration that is 1000x too small and a projected durationSec that is 1000x too large. The code no longer produces new instances.
existingDataNotCorrected.disposition: Reported here as owed data-correction work for whichever chapter owns it, with founder authorization required. NOT scheduled by this unit.

F134.title: Media.aiFlags is client-writable and read by nothing
F134.whatWasWrong: media.service.ts updateMetadata assigned aiFlags WITHOUT the allowUnsafeFields worker gate that protects every neighbouring processed field (thumbnailUrl, displayUrl, playbackUrl, originalUrl).
F134.severityCorrectionRecorded: The finding says aiFlags is 'read by nothing'. That understates it: media.service.ts writes { contentTruthRejection: reason } INTO aiFlags when confirmUpload refuses an object. A client-writable aiFlags therefore let the uploader FORGE or ERASE the record of its own content-truth rejection — the audit trail of the gate that refused it. Recorded as new evidence against F134; the finding text is NOT rewritten and its state is NOT promoted.
F134.change: aiFlags is now gated with the other server-owned fields rather than merely made read-only, so the worker path is unchanged. Caption-class metadata (caption, altText, transcript) stays client-writable — the gate is not a blanket refusal.
